newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen in range, silver to consolidat.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen in range, silver to consolidat.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Gold is expected to remain handcuffed in its recent range of $337.00-$340.00 on Thursday, but will continue to adopt a downside bias against a backdrop of overhead resistance and producer selling, chartists and traders said on Thursday.
Silver was expected to consolidate below $4.80, while platinum was likely to remain firm in nervous trading, they added.
GOLD - Prices were unlikely to move out of their well-worn range of between $337.00 and $340.00 an ounce on Thursday, traders and chartists said.
"Gold is stuck in a range and is showing few signs of breaking out either way," one trader said. Traders expected physical buying on dips and producer selling on any spikes.
Given gold's inability to break above $340.00, downside pressure might emerge.
The recent steady dollar was likely to apply downside pressure.
"Apart from the influence of the dollar, gold is dead in the water," the trader commented.
A break below $336.00 was expected to spark a retracement to $330.00 or $325.00.
Above $340.00 resistance was expected to emerge at $342.00.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was quoted at $337.85/338.15, versus Wednesday's London close of $338.00/$338.50.
SILVER - Seen consolidating below $4.80. Support pegged at $4.60, resistance at $4.80.
At 0820 spot silver was indicated at $4.77/$4.79, against $4.78/$4.80.
PLATINUM - Expected to hold above $410.00. It was last quoted at $418.00/$420.00, against $418.50/$423.50.
